html:
A wagon route of about 3,500 kilometres from the Missouri River to the farmlands of Oregon, used by hundreds of thousands of American settlers between the 1830s and 1869.

Missionaries took wagons over it in 1836. In 1843 about a thousand people made the trip together, and after that the flow grew every year. Families travelled in ox-drawn covered wagons, usually setting out from Independence, Missouri, in spring. The journey took four to six months, across the plains, over the Rocky Mountains at South Pass and along the Snake and Columbia rivers. Disease, above all cholera, killed far more travellers than attacks did.

The trail had branches. The California Trail carried the miners of the gold rush, and the Mormon Trail carried the followers of the Book of Mormon to Utah.

Settlement strengthened the US claim to Oregon, settled with Britain in the Oregon Treaty of 1846. It also brought disease and loss of land to the Native nations along the way. The transcontinental railroad of 1869 made the wagon trail obsolete.
sum: A wagon route of about 3,500 kilometres from the Missouri River to the farmlands of Oregon, used by hundreds of thousands of American settlers between the 1830s and 1869.
